_source.description: Major global magnesium metal production sites (primary magnesium, not magnesite ore)
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, Magnesium Metal chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-magnesium.pdf); International Magnesium Association (IMA) statistical reports (https://www.intlmag.org/); China Magnesium Association (CMA) industry statistics; ICL Group (NYSE: ICL) Annual Report 2023; VSMPO-AVISMA Corporation annual reports; US Magnesium LLC corporate disclosures; Rima Industrial SA corporate publications; UK TMK (Ust-Kamenogorsk Titanium-Magnesium Combine) production reports; Alliance Magnesium Inc. (TSXV: MITE) technical reports; Baotou Xinyuan Magnesium, Shanxi Yinguang Huasheng Magnesium, Ningxia Huiye Magnesium annual reports and government filings
_source.license: USGS: public domain; IMA: membership data fair use summary; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Major magnesium metal production sites globally. This covers primary magnesium metal production (not magnesite mineral mining). China dominates (~87%) via the Pidgeon process (silicothermic reduction of dolomite using ferrosilicon). Non-Chinese production is primarily electrolytic (Dead Sea Magnesium, US Magnesium) or Pidgeon process. Coordinates from company filings, government industrial zone registrations, and satellite verification.

_coverage.known_gaps: Numerous small Chinese Pidgeon process plants not individually enumerated (estimated 50+ small plants across Shanxi, Shaanxi, Ningxia, Inner Mongolia, Henan); some secondary/recycling operations not included; emerging operations in Oman and Malaysia

sites.name: Fugu County (Shaanxi Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple private operators — Shaanxi Fugu Magnesium Industry Zone
sites.notes: World's largest magnesium production district; Fugu County, Yulin prefecture; ~20+ Pidgeon process plants clustered near coal/ferrosilicon supply; produces ~25% of China's Mg output

sites.name: Wenxi County (Shanxi Province)
sites.ownership: Yinguang Huasheng Magnesium Industry Co. and multiple private operators
sites.notes: Major Shanxi Mg production cluster; Wenxi is China's second-largest Mg producing county; Yinguang is one of China's largest individual Mg producers

sites.name: Taiyuan / Qingxu (Shanxi Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple state and private operators in greater Taiyuan area
sites.notes: Northern Shanxi magnesium production zone; multiple medium-scale Pidgeon process plants near Taiyuan industrial corridor

sites.name: Wenshui County (Shanxi Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple operators in Luliang prefecture
sites.notes: Luliang prefecture Mg production area; benefits from local coal and ferrosilicon supply chain

sites.name: Yulin District (Shaanxi Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple private operators in Yulin industrial zone
sites.notes: Broader Yulin area Pidgeon process plants (beyond Fugu cluster); integrated with local coal gasification and ferrosilicon production

sites.name: Ningxia Huiye (Ningxia Hui AR)
sites.ownership: Ningxia Huiye Magnesium & New Material Technology Co.
sites.notes: Yinchuan industrial zone; one of Ningxia's largest magnesium producers; integrated with local ferrosilicon supply

sites.name: Baotou (Inner Mongolia)
sites.ownership: Multiple operators in Baotou industrial zone
sites.notes: Inner Mongolia Mg production; benefits from proximity to dolomite resources and low-cost energy; Baotou is also major rare earth center

sites.name: Sanmenxia (Henan Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple operators in Sanmenxia industrial zone
sites.notes: Western Henan Mg production zone; Pidgeon process plants near Shanxi border; benefits from cross-border dolomite and ferrosilicon supply

sites.name: Jiaocheng County (Shanxi Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple private Pidgeon process operators
sites.notes: Taiyuan-area Mg production cluster in Jiaocheng County; part of broader central Shanxi magnesium belt

sites.name: Wuzhong (Ningxia Hui AR)
sites.ownership: Multiple operators
sites.notes: Southern Ningxia Mg production area; smaller-scale Pidgeon process operations

sites.name: Qinghai Mg Pilot (Qinghai Province)
sites.operator: Qinghai Salt Lake Industry / state enterprises
sites.ownership: Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co. (partially state-owned)
sites.notes: Pilot electrolytic Mg production from Qaidam Basin salt lake brines; targets lower-emission production pathway; government-supported strategic project; 100,000 tpa target for full-scale phase

sites.name: Dead Sea Magnesium (Sodom)
sites.ownership: ICL Group (TASE: ICL / NYSE: ICL) — 65%; Volkswagen AG — 35%
sites.notes: One of only two large-scale electrolytic Mg producers globally; near Arad/Sodom; produces pure Mg and alloys from Dead Sea carnallite; Volkswagen JV partner for automotive Mg

sites.name: Berezniki (Perm Krai)
sites.ownership: VSMPO-AVISMA Corporation (Rostec subsidiary)
sites.notes: AVISMA titanium-magnesium works; produces Mg as co-product with titanium sponge; one of world's largest titanium producers; Perm Krai; electrolytic process using Verkhnekamskoye potash deposit carnallite

sites.name: Solikamsk (Perm Krai)
sites.ownership: SMW (Solikamskiy Magnievyy Zavod)
sites.notes: One of Russia's oldest Mg plants (operating since 1936); electrolytic process; also produces rare earth concentrates from loparite; adjacent to Verkhnekamskoye potash deposits

sites.name: Ust-Kamenogorsk (East Kazakhstan)
sites.ownership: UK TMK JSC (state-controlled via Tau-Ken Samruk)
sites.notes: Soviet-era titanium-magnesium combine; produces Mg as co-product with titanium sponge; electrolytic process; East Kazakhstan region; major CIS Mg supplier

sites.name: US Magnesium (Great Salt Lake, Utah)
sites.ownership: US Magnesium LLC (private; Renco Group)
sites.notes: Only primary Mg producer in the Western Hemisphere; Rowley, Tooele County, UT; electrolytic process extracting MgCl2 from Great Salt Lake brine; strategic US domestic supply

sites.name: Rima Industrial (Bocaiuva, Minas Gerais)
sites.ownership: Rima Industrial SA (private Brazilian company)
sites.notes: Latin America's largest and only major Mg producer; Pidgeon process using local dolomite and charcoal-based ferrosilicon; Bocaiuva, northern Minas Gerais

sites.name: Kayseri (Central Anatolia)
sites.ownership: Multiple private Turkish companies
sites.notes: Central Anatolia Mg production using local dolomite; emerging Turkish Pidgeon process operations; Kayseri industrial zone

sites.name: Biga (Canakkale Province)
sites.ownership: Various operators in Marmara region
sites.notes: Northwestern Turkey Mg production; Canakkale province; smaller-scale Pidgeon process operations using Biga Peninsula dolomite resources

sites.name: Porsgrunn (Telemark)
sites.ownership: Formerly Norsk Hydro ASA (OSE: NHY)
sites.notes: Norsk Hydro's historic Mg electrolysis plant; operated 1951-2002; closed due to Chinese competition; site retained for potential restart; Hydro shifted to recycled Mg

sites.name: Alliance Magnesium (Danville, Quebec)
sites.ownership: Alliance Magnesium Inc. (TSXV: MITE)
sites.notes: Novel process extracting Mg from asbestos mine serpentine tailings in Danville, Quebec (former Asbestos region); demonstration plant operational; targeting full-scale 11,500 tpa Phase 1; government-supported for strategic Mg supply

sites.name: Qingyuan (Liaoning Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple private operators
sites.notes: Northeastern China Mg production cluster; Liaoning Province; smaller-scale operations using local dolomite and ferrosilicon

sites.name: Haicheng (Liaoning Province)
sites.ownership: Multiple operators in Anshan-Haicheng industrial zone
sites.notes: Haicheng is China's largest magnesite producing area; some operators also produce Mg metal via Pidgeon process; Liaoning Province; dual magnesite/Mg metal production zone

sites.name: Zaporozhye (Zaporizhzhia)
sites.ownership: ZTMC (state-owned, United Chemical Company Ukrhimtransammiak)
sites.notes: Soviet-era titanium-magnesium combine; operations disrupted since 2022 conflict; historically produced ~10,000 tpa Mg as co-product with titanium sponge

sites.name: Yeongju (North Gyeongsang)
sites.ownership: POSCO and Korean industrial partners
sites.notes: South Korean strategic Mg supply project; POSCO exploring domestic production to reduce China dependency; pilot/development stage

sites.name: Becancour (Quebec)
sites.ownership: Various; industrial zone includes former Norsk Hydro/Magnola site
sites.notes: Site of former Norsk Hydro Magnola plant (closed 2003); various proposals for restart/new electrolytic Mg production in Becancour industrial park; Quebec hydropower advantage

sites.name: Kuqa (Xinjiang Uyghur AR)
sites.ownership: Various operators in Kuqa industrial zone
sites.notes: Western China Mg production; Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region; utilizes local coal and dolomite resources; smaller-scale operations

sites.name: Shandong Mg Cluster (Linyi)
sites.ownership: Multiple private operators in Linyi area
sites.notes: Eastern China Mg production cluster; Shandong Province; some alloy production for automotive/die-casting market; relatively small by Chinese standards
